title: Graduate - P&O - Geoscience - AZ
description:
Job Family Group:

Business Support Group, Subsurface Group


Job Description:

Early Careers at bp

Looking to turn your career dreams into global impact? Explore graduate opportunities with bp. Here you get to work on challenging projects, learn from experts and mentors, and be part of a high-performing team from the get-go. You get the freedom to think boldly, the licence to innovate and the chance to grow in multiple directions. And you get supported, recognised and rewarded along the way.

Our Geoscience Graduate Programme

One Sciences is our Early Careers programme designed to create a pipeline of science talent, positioned to lead bp through the energy transition, to provide reliable, affordable and lower carbon energy to the world and achieve net-zero. The program is 3 years, with most early careers completing three 12-month rotations, designed to provide breadth of experience and build technical depth.

Early careers will follow a structured development offer to accelerate the acquisition of foundational technical skills, experience and knowledge; and application in the business world. The programme supports transition from university to discipline professional and, through our 'Elevate' training programme, provides a framework of ‘non-technical’ skills to support building personal effectiveness, helping you to grow both personally and professionally.

Early careers will build their experience through challenging development assignments, grow a toolkit of transferable skills for the future, and have a dedicated network of support, as well as a vibrant Early Careers community, to help them succeed.

Role and Responsibilities

Job description for Geophysics Graduate role

Geophysicist role will require the individual to be able to learn and operate with relevant support from senior members of the team in seismic interpretation, analysis, and integration of geophysical data with other disciplines supporting well concept and early well design squads. The Geophysicist will support the integrated subsurface description (ISD), special studies and New Well Delivery activities and practices as it relates to the New Well Delivery common process. They will interface with drilling and completions teams to create well documents to pass D1, D2, D3 (WID) and D5 (SOR) and D11 (Subsurface end of well reports) Stages. They may be asked to provide geophysical operational support as needed. They may represent bp externally or in partner meetings.

The following accountabilities are generic and will be subject to clarity depending on where Graduate Geophysicist will be assigned to:

  • As an individual technical contributor, working closely with other subsurface disciplines, you will deliver high-quality geophysical inputs to progress prioritized business opportunities.

  • You will interpret and integrate seismic, well-log, analogue, and dynamic data (pressure, production etc.) to develop and refine the integrated structural, stratigraphic, depositional, rock property and fluid frameworks that underpin integrated subsurface products.

  • Part of an integrated team which delivers all the required reservoir geophysical inputs, documents and reviews for the well planning and deliver process from D1, D2 to D5.

  • Contributes to the delivery of all the required geophysical inputs to well planning and execution (D2-D5) including real time activity within Integrated Well Delivery. Emphasis is on understanding the relevant practices.

  • Learns how to provide the most up-to-date geophysical information as input to the generation of all maps and other internal documents whilst adhering to defined practices engaging the discipline lead and other field geophysicists as needed for assurance.

  • Learns how to identify strengths, weaknesses, threats and opportunities found whilst analyzing the data.

  • Works with senior geophysicists to identity studies, projects and programs to improve or understand the data.

  • Works with other geophysicists in ADU teams to deliver products for reservoir characterization and to analyze these products.

  • Works with other disciplines to ensure that a consistent truly integrated subsurface description of the field is maintained and input to key documents. Emphasis here will be on the individual learning how to deliver these products.

  • You are expected to learn how to use best practice workflows and to continually search for new and improved ways of generating seismic products and the interpretation of these through interaction with Central Technology teams, Seismic Delivery teams and other technical experts.

  • Will take an active part in community sessions and may be a local representative for a community of practice.

  • Build organizational capability through knowledge sharing and coaching of summer interns.

  • You will participates in informing all stakeholders and other disciplines of ongoing changes to the geophysical understanding and new geophysical products.

  • Contributes to sharing geophysical understanding of the field with SOCAR, Partners and others as needed (e.g., inputs to RMWG meetings)

  • Working constructively with Discipline Leader and others to build and implement a personal development plan.

Job description for Petrophysics Graduate role

Do you have a passion for solving puzzles? Can you think differently about data? These are the kind of things we look for in a bp Petrophysicist. Petrophysicists play a crucial role in our efforts to produce enough oil and gas to help satisfy the world’s growing demand for energy. At bp, our Petrophysicists define the volume and distribution of oil and gas in our reservoirs as well as their flow characteristics. They investigate the quality of reservoir rocks such as their porosity, permeability and how reservoir fluids interact with the reservoir matrix. This involves the integration of direct measurements of reservoir properties, from core and fluid samples extracted from the reservoir together with data from sophisticated indirect measurements made by logging tools lowered into boreholes. These tools measure the nuclear, electrical and acoustic response of rocks and the integrated results are used to predict the volume and distribution of the hydrocarbons and optimise the methods of extraction.

As a Petrophysicist graduate joining our multi-disciplinary and multicultural subsurface team, you’ll work on our global exploration program, new field developments or at a producing asset - all dynamic, collaborative environments. You’ll interact with geoscientists; reservoir, petroleum and drilling engineers; as well as commercial and other disciplines to turn your evaluations into business decisions and actions.

Requirements

  • Azerbaijani citizenship
  • Relevant bachelor’s and/or master’s degree
  • 2025, 2026 and 2027 academic year graduates are eligible to apply
  • CGPA 75% (2.5)

Specializations:

  • Geoscience - Geophysics
  • Geoscience - Other
  • Biostratigraphy
  • Earth Science
  • Petrophysics
  • Geomechanics

description:

title: Community Home Lending Officer
description:
First Merchants is seeking a Community Home Lending Officer to join our team! The Community Home Lending Officer (CHLO) is responsible for originating residential mortgage loans while expanding access to sustainable homeownership through community engagement, financial education, and relationship development. This role develops new business through partnerships with real estate professionals, employers, housing agencies, community organizations, and other referral sources. The CHLO serves as a trusted advisor by educating customers on mortgage products, down payment assistance programs, affordable lending solutions, and the homebuying process. Successful candidates demonstrate strong business development and relationship management skills, deliver an exceptional customer experience, and achieve consistent production results. They maintain a well-managed pipeline, collaborate effectively with internal and external partners, and adhere to all applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements while supporting the Bank's commitment to expanding homeownership opportunities within the communities it serves. This position is subject to the Dodd-Frank Act and Truth in Lending Act qualification requirements for Mortgage Loan Originators. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of all applicable background, credit, and NMLS-related requirements.

As part of this role you will:

  • Develop new mortgage business through networking, prospecting, and cultivating relationships with real estate professionals, builders, community organizations, employers, internal referral partners, and prospective homebuyers.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor by educating customers on available mortgage products, down payment assistance programs, affordable lending programs, and the homebuying process.
  • Interview applicants, analyze financial information, take residential mortgage applications, and ensure complete and accurate loan submissions.
  • Maintain knowledge of residential mortgage products, down payment assistance programs, affordable lending programs, underwriting guidelines, regulatory requirements, and market conditions.
  • Build and maintain partnerships with community organizations, real estate professionals, employers, housing agencies, and other referral sources to identify homeownership opportunities, expand access to sustainable homeownership, and support the Bank's community engagement initiatives.
  • Plan, coordinate, and deliver homebuyer education workshops, financial education presentations, and community outreach events in support of Community Home Lending and Bank community service goals.
  • Participate in community activities and professional organizations to strengthen community relationships, enhance the Bank's visibility, and create opportunities to serve prospective homebuyers.
  • Demonstrate operational excellence by maintaining a well-managed pipeline, ensuring timely follow-up, accurate and complete loan applications, collaborating effectively with internal and external partners, and adhering to bank policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Deliver an exceptional customer experience throughout the mortgage lending process.
  • Achieve individual production goals and contribute to overall Community Home Lending team objectives.
  • Serve as an ambassador for First Merchants Bank by representing the Bank professionally in all customer, community, and business interactions.

To be successful in this position, we require the following:

  • High school diploma or equivalent (GED).
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in mortgage lending, mortgage origination, consumer lending with mortgage referral responsibilities, or a related residential lending role.
  • Active NMLS registration and ability to maintain eligibility for mortgage loan originator registration under applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Experience achieving sales, production, or business development goals.
  • Experience independently developing and managing a pipeline of mortgage lending opportunities.
  • Experience analyzing borrower financial information and recommending appropriate lending solutions.
  • Experience educating customers on financial products and services, guiding customers through the lending process, and supporting homeownership opportunities.

    The following would be a plus:

    • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Communications, Marketing, or a related field.

    • Experience working with down payment assistance programs, affordable lending programs, or other homeownership initiatives.

    • Experience developing partnerships with community organizations, real estate professionals, employers, housing agencies, or other referral sources.

    • Experience delivering homebuyer education, financial education programs, or community outreach events.

    First Merchants offers the following:

    • Base Pay PLUS Bonuses
    • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
    • 401k
    • Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts
    • Vacation/Sick Time
    • Paid Holidays
    • Paid Parental Leave
    • Tuition Reimbursement
    • Additional Benefits

    A little about us:

    First Merchants is guided by a genuine philosophy of being a meaningful place to work and having a prosperous impact across all walks of life throughout the communities we serve, including consumers, businesses and other organizations. Our Vision, Mission and Team statement reflect and reinforce that authentic service philosophy.

    Our Vision is:

    To enhance the financial wellness of the diverse communities we serve.

    Our Mission is:

    To be the most responsive, knowledgeable, and high-performing financial organization for our clients, teammates, and shareholders.

    Our Team:

    "We are a collection of dynamic colleagues with diverse experiences and perspectives who share a passion for positively impacting lives. We are genuinely committed to attracting and engaging teammates of diverse backgrounds. We believe in the power of inclusion and belonging."

    Apply today to begin your career with us!

  • Build monitoring and observability solutions capable of processing large volumes of production signals and converting them into actionable insights.
  • Configure and optimize Kubernetes infrastructure for high availability, scalability, and efficient resource utilization.
  • Tune Kubernetes autoscaling mechanisms to improve the efficiency and utilization of GPU resources.
  • Develop and maintain Terraform modules and infrastructure-as-code patterns that embed resilience and reliability into new clusters and services.
  • Design and improve request-routing, retry, and failure-handling mechanisms to minimize the impact of transient infrastructure or service failures.
  • Develop automation and operational tooling to detect, isolate, and remediate incidents quickly.
  • Create, maintain, and improve runbooks for incident response and operational procedures.
  • Participate in production incident management, troubleshooting issues and restoring services within demanding reliability objectives.
  • Lead or contribute to post-mortem processes and implement corrective actions to prevent recurring incidents.
  • Define and improve reliability practices for high-throughput APIs, including alerting strategies and Service Level Objectives (SLOs).
  • Investigate distributed-system failures and performance issues across infrastructure and application layers.
  • Optimize systems from the kernel and infrastructure layer through to the application layer.
  • Support and improve the operation of GPU-intensive inference workloads and accelerator-based infrastructure.
  • Contribute to scaling the inference platform while balancing performance, reliability, and infrastructure costs.
  • Collaborate closely with software engineers to incorporate reliability and operational excellence into product and platform development.
  • Promote automation, self-healing capabilities, and engineering practices that reduce operational overhead and improve system resilience.

    • Requirements:

    • Significant experience in Site Reliability Engineering, Production Engineering, DevOps, or a closely related infrastructure discipline.
    • Deep practical knowledge of Kubernetes in production environments.
    • Strong experience with Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring, metrics, dashboards, and observability.
    • Advanced experience with Terraform and infrastructure-as-code practices.
    • Strong scripting and automation skills using Python and/or Bash.
    • Solid understanding of distributed systems and the ways production backends can fail under real-world conditions.
    • Experience designing effective alerts, monitoring strategies, and SLOs for high-throughput services or APIs.
    • Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills across infrastructure, networking, operating systems, and application layers.
    • Experience designing systems for high availability, resilience, scalability, and graceful failure recovery.
    • Hands-on experience with GPU-heavy workloads or accelerator-based infrastructure is highly valuable.

    • Strong understanding of infrastructure automation, deployment, configuration management, and operational tooling.
    • Ability to analyze complex performance and reliability problems and translate findings into practical engineering improvements.

title: Psychiatrist FT - Crisis Care Centers
description:
Psychiatrist - Crisis Care Center Full-time



Under the supervision of the Medical Director, the Psychiatrist will perform clinical duties and activities as directed, covering the continuum of intensive crisis stabilization services (ICSS) including Crisis Stabilization Unit, Behavioral Health Urgent Care, and Mobile Crisis Services.



PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:



  • Flexibility in scheduling. The standard schedule is generally during daytime hours, with alternative scheduling options available, including longer shifts, as mutually agreed upon in alignment with clinical and program needs.
  • Flexibility to incorporate work across a variety of clinical settings within the organization based on the psychiatrist’s interests and preferences, in alignment with program needs.
  • Provides direct clinical/patient care duties and responsibilities as required, including psychiatric evaluation, re-evaluation, disposition, coordination of medical services with nurse on duty, medication orders/prescribing, restraint orders, monitoring patients, etc.
  • Incorporates Evidenced Based Best Practice Standards into service delivery.
  • Provides care compliant with licensing regulations and accreditation standards.
  • Determines medical necessity.
  • Provides expertise on medical topics such as psychotropic medication, psychiatric evaluation, coordination of care, etc.
  • Supervises coordination of care activities.
  • Oversees discharge planning.
  • Completes clinical documentation as required.
  • Oversees and provides clinical supervision to Advanced Practice Providers; collaborates, discusses cases, and co-signs notes.
  • Provides supervision and direction to the mobile crisis team.
  • Completes doctor-to-doctor communications, as necessary.
  • Reviews Eligibility assessments for members contacting the Crisis Care Center.
  • Completes required trainings.
  • Teaches students and Psychiatry residents and fellows, as appropriate.
  • Participates in clinical and administrative meetings.
  • Participates in Quality Assurance reviews.
  • Initiates and/or continues emergency medication orders or restraints in accordance with state law.
  • Collaborates with an interdisciplinary team to continuously improve productivity, efficiency, recovery outcomes, and medical care.
  • Handles work responsibilities and challenges with honest and ethical behavior.
  • Ensures appropriate responses to all medical emergencies.
  • Provides clinical coverage and consultation on any urgent clinical issue that may arise between the time that members contact the Crisis Care Center and/or Mobile Crisis Team and until they are seen by our Clinically Responsible Service Providers.
  • Attends shift handover meetings.
  • Participates in on-call weekend coverage rotation as indicated.
  • Understands and adheres to DWIHN compliance standards as they appear in the Code of Conduct and Conflict of Interest Policies.
  • Maintains patient confidentiality per federal guidelines and DWIHN policy and procedures.
  • Identifies and timely reports any health and safety risks, accidents, incidents, injuries, and property damage at the workplace.
  • Performs any additional duties as assigned by the Medical Director.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES (KSA’S):

  • Knowledge and experience with the Accreditation and Certification Standards Joint Commission.
  • Knowledge of DWIHN policies, procedures, and practices.
  • Knowledge of the DWIHN provider network and community resources.
  • Knowledge of the Michigan Mental Health Code.
  • Knowledge of MDHHS policies, rules, regulations, and procedures.
  • Knowledge of Federal policies, rules, regulations, and procedures as it relates to DWIHN.
  • Knowledge and ability to work with agitated patients in crisis and their families to implement behavioral management interventions.
  • Knowledge of the clinical care process (screening, assessment, treatment planning, case management, and continuing care).
  • Knowledge of and ability to use screening and assessment tools for behavioral health services.
  • Knowledge of medical and behavioral health practices and terminology.
  • Knowledge of compliance standards.
  • Knowledge of Medical Necessity Criteria for Behavioral Health Services.
  • Knowledge of documents/regulations that govern the provision of mental health services, e.g., Medicaid Manual Mental Health and Substance Abuse Chapter III, State Plan for Medicaid, Michigan Department of Health and Human Services Quality Plan, BBA requirements, and the Mental Health Code.
  • Knowledge of the practices and principles of psychological, emotional, and sociological assessment and diagnosis.
  • Knowledge of diagnostics, psychopharmacology, and supportive treatment approaches as applied to a severely mentally ill (SMI) population.
  • Knowledge of the identification and treatment of co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders.
  • Knowledge of psychotropic medications.
  • Knowledge of Community Mental Health Services Programs (CMHSP) and Prepaid Inpatient Health Plans (PIHP).
  • Knowledge of community mental health services and resources.
  • Knowledge of the DSM-V Statistical Manual.
  • Leadership skills.
  • Training skills.
  • Assessment and evaluation skills.
  • Organizational skills.
  • Attention to detail skills.
  • Planning skills.
  • Analytical skills.
  • Clinical documentation skills.
  • Report writing skills.
  • Decision making skills.
  • Critical thinking skills.
  • Interpersonal skills.
  • Effective listening skills
  • Communication skills.
  • Teaching skills.
  • Computer skills (Word, Excel, Access, Power Point, Outlook, Teams)
  • Teamwork skills.
  • Ability to communicate orally.
  • Ability to communicate in writing.
  • Ability to work effectively with others.
  • Ability to work with an ethnically, linguistically, culturally, economically, and socially diverse population.
  • Judgment/reasoning ability.

REQUIRED EDUCATION:

A Medical Degree from an accredited School of Medicine.

Board Certification in Psychiatry by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology.

NOTE: Additional Board Certification in Addiction Psychiatry and/or Child and Adolescent Psychiatry is preferred.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:

Two (2) years of professional experience in the treat­ment of behavioral health problems.

REQUIRED LICENSES:

  • A valid and current Michigan License to practice as a physician.
  • A valid and current Michigan controlled substance license.
  • A valid and current Drug Enforcement Agency Registration.
  • A valid State of Michigan Driver’s License with a safe and acceptable driving record.



WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is usually performed at the Crisis Care Center but may require the employee to drive to different sites throughout Wayne County and the State of Michigan.

title: Senior Scientist, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, Q.InC
description:
We are seeking a Senior Scientist to lead the development of quantum sensing platforms based on atomic vapor cell systems, with an emphasis on precision magnetometry and inertial sensing. The successful candidate will be required to undertake the following key tasks of the project:

  • Contribute to technical reports, manuscripts, grant proposals, and project documentation.

Qualification and Field of Study:

PhD in Physics, Applied Physics, Quantum Science, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related discipline

title: Production Worker
description:
Goodwill Industries of Hawaii, Inc.

Job Title: Production Worker

At Goodwill, we do more than provide jobs — we create pathways to opportunity and dignity through the power of work. Our mission-driven culture sets us apart, and every role directly supports individuals in achieving self-sufficiency and success. When you join Goodwill, you're not just building a career — you're changing lives.

So, join the Goodwill Hawaii family and help strengthen our community, one job at a time!

SUMMARY


The Production Worker inspects donated items for defects and determines their appropriate outcome based on established quality standards. A Production Worker’s responsibilities include sorting, pricing, tagging, and preparing both textile and non-textile items for sale, recycling, or disposal. The Production Worker requires meeting daily production quotas while maintaining a low error rate, adhering to safety protocols, and being available to work on weekends.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following.


  • Removes item from bins or carts for close inspection to determine if item is saleable.
  • Scans clothing/textile items for defects such as holes, rips, tears, misaligned or missing fasteners or trim, and variations in color of fabric for clothing items. Examines fabric for holes or stains. Sorts textiles to determine quality and price or if item goes to As-Is, bale, or dump if appropriate
  • For non-clothing items, scans items for defects such as cracks, rust, broken or missing pieces, stains, and if item is operational. Sort and price item accordingly. Cleans item as needed.
  • Hangs, tags, and prices textile and non-textile items.
  • Works at different work stations as production needs require or stocking as needs arises.
  • Must meet the following production standards:

• Grade and sort 2.5 carts or 486 units per hour with an error rate of less than 5%.

• Complete (sort, hang, tag) ½ of a rack of clothing per hour or complete (sort, price) 4 totes of non-textile items per hour.

  • Conducts work in a safe and responsible manner utilizing protective clothing and equipment and complies with safety standards.
  • Responsible for awareness of and adherence to all company and safety policies and procedures.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Employees are regularly required to:

  • stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel;
  • reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear.
  • frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
  • occasionally maneuver wheeled containers weighing up to 100 pounds



WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to outside weather condition and heat. The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, including gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, age, marital status, genetic information, domestic or sexual violence victim status, disability, protected veteran status or any other status protected by federal, state or local law. title: Partner Rep, Intersport France
description:

The Partner Rep will work closely with several cross-functional teams within Nike, including Planning, Marketing, Merchandising, Finance, and Operations, to ensure the seamless execution of Nike’s sales strategy.

title: Tool Crib Attendant
description:
TOOL CRIB ATTENDANT

Summary: The Tool Crib Attendant is responsible for the controlled management, traceability, and continuous improvement of tooling, gauges, and manufacturing support equipment within an aerospace and defense production environment. This role ensures full compliance with applicable quality standards, customer requirements, and internal procedures while supporting safe, efficient, and repeatable manufacturing operations. Serving as a key support function to Production, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain, the Tool Crib Attendant safeguards tooling integrity, maintains accurate records, and contributes to cost control, risk mitigation, and new product introduction activities. Attention to detail, adherence to established processes, and sound judgment are critical to success in this role.

Job Responsibilities

Tooling Control & Traceability

  • Manage controlled inventories of cutting tools, holders, gauges, fixtures, and production support equipment
  • Ensure tooling traceability in accordance with aerospace and defense quality standards (e.g., AS9100, customer flow-downs)
  • Control issuance, return, life tracking, and segregation of tooling to prevent damage, loss, or misuse
  • Support FOD (Foreign Object Debris) prevention through disciplined tool control practices

Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure tooling and gauges meet calibration, inspection, and certification requirements
  • Maintain accurate records to support audits, internal inspections, and customer or regulatory reviews
  • Ensure compliance with internal procedures, quality manuals, and work instructions
  • Support corrective and preventive actions related to tooling or equipment issues

Purchasing & Cost Management

  • Provide tooling usage data, forecasts, and budget input to Purchasing and Management
  • Review and support blanket order requirements, tooling lead times, and supplier performance
  • Evaluate tooling pricing, life expectancy, and standardization opportunities in collaboration with Engineering
  • Support cost reduction initiatives without compromising quality or compliance

Manufacturing & Engineering Support

  • Perform precision measurement and verification of specialized tooling using vernier calipers, micrometers, and dial test indicators
  • Create and maintain tool kits and carts aligned with production cells, routings, and work orders
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI), first article inspections (FAI), and production ramp-ups through tooling readiness
  • Participate in tooling trials, process improvements, and engineering change implementation

Systems, Processes & Leadership

  • Operate and manage automated or matrix tool distribution systems
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve tool crib procedures and documentation
  • Train and mentor tool crib staff and production personnel on proper tooling handling and control
  • Promote a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement


Qualifications & Requirements

Education

  • College diploma required

Experience

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in a tool crib or tooling control role within a regulated manufacturing environment

Technical Skills

  • In-depth knowledge of aerospace-grade cutting tools, holders, and tooling systems
  • Proficiency with precision measurement instruments including vernier calipers, micrometers, and dial test indicators
  • Experience with Zoeller or equivalent automated tool vending systems considered an asset
  • Experience managing matrix or controlled tool distribution systems

Additional Requirements

  • Strong understanding of quality systems and documentation discipline
  • Ability to work effectively in an AS9100 / ISO-certified environment
  • Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and professionalism in a defense-related environment

title: Quality Control - Microbiologist
description:
Microbiologist

ScaleUp Bio | Singapore

Role Overview

Microbiology professional with experience in microbiological testing, environmental monitoring, contamination control, laboratory operations, GMP compliance, and audit support. Participates in internal, customer, and regulatory audits to ensure inspection readiness and adherence to quality and regulatory requirements in a GMP regulated CDMO manufacturing environment.

About ScaleUpBio

ScaleUp Bio is a Singapore-based precision fermentation CDMO focused on enabling the scale-up and manufacture of high-value bio-based specialty molecules. The company provides integrated process development, pilot scale-up and manufacturing capabilities to support customers from development through commercial production. Serving applications across multiple industries, ScaleUp Bio is positioned to help address the growing global need for high-quality fermentation infrastructure.

Role Overview

ScaleUp Bio is seeking a technically competent Microbiologist to support Microbiological testing, Environmental monitoring, contamination control, and Laboratory operations.

The role is responsible for ensuring microbiological quality and compliance across raw materials, manufacturing processes, utilities, controlled environments, In-process and finished products.

The ideal candidate is hands-on, quality-focused, and capable of working effectively within a multidisciplinary team, supporting biotechnology and fermentation-based manufacturing operations. This individual should be comfortable operating in a manufacturing area while maintaining high standards of laboratory discipline, and regulatory compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Microbiological Testing

  • Prepare and maintain working cell banks, vials.
  • Perform routine microbiological testing of raw materials, in-process samples, finished products, utilities (water, compressed air, and steam), and environmental monitoring samples.
  • Conduct microbial limit testing, bioburden testing, sterility testing, and other microbiological analyses as required.
  • Perform microbial identification using conventional and rapid microbiological methods.
  • Prepare, qualify, and maintain microbiological media, reagents, standards, and laboratory supplies.
  • Review and verify microbiological test results for accuracy, completeness, and compliance.

Environmental Monitoring

  • Execute environmental monitoring programs for cleanrooms and controlled manufacturing area.
  • Collect, analyse, and document air, surface, personnel, water, and utility monitoring samples.
  • Trend environmental monitoring data and identify potential contamination risks and adverse trends.
  • Support investigations related to environmental monitoring excursions, out-of-limit results, and contamination events.
  • Contribute to contamination control strategies and continuous monitoring improvements.

Quality & Compliance

  • Ensure all laboratory activities comply with GMP, GLP, data integrity requirements and SOP’s.
  • Review & maintain laboratory reports, test results, logs, worksheets, and documentation.
  • Participate in deviation investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA implementation, change controls, and RA.
  • Support internal audits, customer audits, supplier audits, and regulatory inspections.

Laboratory Operations & Equipment Management

  • Operate, maintain, and perform routine checks on microbiological laboratory equipment, which includes: Biosafety Cabinets, Shaker Incubators, Autoclaves, Deep Freezers, Incubators, Colony Counters, Analytical Balances, Spectrophotometers, Moisture Analyser, HPLC, 10L glass reactor and other analytical instruments, as required
  • Support equipment qualification, calibration coordination, preventive maintenance, and troubleshooting activities.
  • Operate and monitor 10 L glass reactor systems for pilot-scale fermentation, microbial cultivation, ensuring compliance with established procedures and safety requirements.
  • Assist in method validation, verification, and technology transfer activities.
  • Monitor laboratory inventory and coordinate procurement of microbiological consumables and reagents.
  • Maintain laboratory cleanliness, organization, and biosafety standards.

Technical Support & Continuous Improvement

  • Provide microbiological expertise to Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Process Development, and Pilot Scale Manufacturing teams.
  • Support contamination investigations and root cause analyses for microbiological events.
  • Assist in developing, reviewing, and revising SOPs, protocols, specifications, and technical reports.
  • Support process optimization and continuous improvement initiatives related to microbiology and contamination control.
  • Contribute to the implementation of new microbiological technologies and laboratory best practices.

Requirements

  • Ability to take on day-shifts during peak plant utilization.
  • Diploma/Bachelor's Degree in Microbiology / Biotechnology / Life Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 - 5 years of relevant microbiology laboratory experience.
  • Experience in food manufacturing, fermentation, life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, or related industries preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of microbiological testing techniques, aseptic practices.
  • Able to work independently with GMP, GLP, data integrity requirements, and quality management systems.
  • Experience with environmental monitoring programs and cleanroom operations is advantageous.
  • Strong documentation, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Flexible to work weekends, shifts, or overtime as required by operational needs.

Preferred Attributes

  • Strong commitment to quality.
  • Hands-on experience with lab equipment with excellent aseptic technique.
  • Proactive and solution-oriented approach to problem solving.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and compliance.
  • Collaborative team player capable of working across functions.
  • Committed to continuous learning and professional development.

title: Assistant Innkeeper
description:
Start your mornings at the historic Timberholm Inn! Since 1949, our bed & breakfast has welcomed travelers, adventurers, and families alike, offering a slice of history with the ambiance of a bygone era. Recognized by the Stowe Historical Society as one of the original ski lodges of the area, Timberholm continues to be a cherished destination year-round.
We are seeking a detail-oriented and guest-focused Assistant Innkeeper to create memorable
morning experiences for guests at our 9-room boutique bed and breakfast. This role is ideal for
someone who enjoys the art of breakfast, thrives in a collaborative team environment, and takes
pride in creating seamless, personalized experiences for guests from first contact to their next stay.
Training will be provided, along with ongoing support during the transition and beyond. If you have
a passion for cooking or baking, a keen eye for cleanliness, and a welcoming personality, we would
love to have you join our team.
Days: 2 mornings per week, Thursday & Sunday
Shift Length: 4 hours
Standard Hours: 7:00 AM – 11:00 AM, breakfast served at 8:00 am
Ski Season Hours: 6:00 AM - 10:00 AM, breakfast served at 7:00 am

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Arrive early to prep ingredients and bake/cook high-quality breakfast items for guests.
  • Lay out and maintain the buffet breakfast selection throughout the service window.
  • Label and communicate allergy/special dietary needs foods clearly.
  • Brew coffee and have hot water available for tea/hot chocolate.
  • Examples of prepared breakfast items include: scrambled eggs, pancakes, waffles, bacon.
  • Restock coffee and tea stations throughout the morning.
  • Keep fridge items, snacks, and beverage stations fully replenished for the day ahead.
  • Communicate any low-inventory items or kitchen needs to leadership.
  • Greet guests warmly and exhibit a high standard of hospitality and professionalism.
  • Interact with guests during breakfast, answering basic questions about Timberholm and the surrounding areas and making them feel welcome.
  • Address guest inquiries or dietary needs during service with care and professionalism.
  • Coordinate closely with Hannah on any special requests or guest/inn concerns.
  • Resolve minor guest issues and escalate to the leadership team when necessary.
  • Efficiently handle all breakfast cleanup, including washing dishes, sanitizing cookware, and clearing tables.
  • Mop the kitchen floor and thoroughly vacuum the Great Room after service concludes.
  • Ensure all remaining food is properly stored, labeled, and put away according to food safety standards.
  • Coordinate regularly with Hannah/broader team on critical guest and inn related items.
  • Support a positive, communicative, and team-oriented work environment

Requirements

  • Authorized to work in the United States
  • Ability to communicate in English, both written and verbal
  • Valid state issued driver’s license and current auto insurance
  • Basic computer skills
  • Comply with all company policies and procedures
  • Exemplify a high-performance culture through words and actions
  • Present a positive image as the face of Timberholm Inn in the market, industry, and our community.
  • Hospitality-minded with a focus on delivering excellent guest experiences
  • Strong communicator with a warm, friendly demeanor
  • Dependable for early mornings and twice weekly shifts
  • Problem-solver who can handle guest concerns with professionalism
  • Detail oriented and uses time efficiently
  • Physical stamina to stand for long periods, bend, lift, and handle tasks such as mopping and vacuuming
Given the unique nature of the company and our strong focus on integrity and values, these cultural components of how we operate will be continually re-enforced. Timberholm Inn maintains the highest professional standards and pledges to operate with integrity and honesty in all that we do. Timberholm Inn strives to always put our guests first, choosing to do what is in their best interest even if that choice may not be the easy or popular path. We believe in a collaborative environment between the administrative staff, leadership, and all members of the Timberholm Inn staff. We recognize that everyone has a voice, realizing that the status quo can be improved upon based on our unique and diverse capabilities and insights. We embrace diversity realizing the benefit of working together and sharing individual insights with the group. Through these ideas discovered in the pursuit of solving problems, we will improve results both for our guests and ourselves. We strive to be able to say to each other, “We didn’t just support each other, we made each other better professionally.”

The Cutter - Fabrication plays a critical role in the manufacturing process by accurately cutting materials to specified dimensions, ensuring the foundation for high-quality fabricated products. This position requires precision and attention to detail to meet design specifications and maintain production efficiency. The Cutter collaborates closely with fabrication and production teams to prepare materials that meet safety and quality standards. By effectively managing cutting equipment and interpreting technical drawings, the Cutter contributes to minimizing waste and optimizing material usage. Ultimately, this role supports the seamless flow of the fabrication process, directly impacting the overall success of production operations.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Proven experience operating cutting machinery in a fabrication or manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and blueprints.
  • Strong attention to detail and manual dexterity.
  • Basic math skills for measuring and calculating material dimensions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certification or training in fabrication or machining.
  • Familiarity with safety standards and regulations in manufacturing settings.
  • Previous experience working in a team-oriented production environment.
  • Basic computer skills for tracking production data and inventory.

Responsibilities:

  • Interpret and analyze blueprints, technical drawings, and cutting instructions to determine material requirements and cutting specifications.
  • Operate cutting machinery such as shears, saws, and automated cutting systems safely and efficiently to produce components according to specifications.
  • Measure and mark materials accurately before cutting to ensure precision and adherence to quality standards.
  • Inspect cut materials for defects or deviations and report any issues to supervisors for corrective action.
  • Maintain cutting equipment by performing routine cleaning, lubrication, and minor adjustments to ensure optimal performance.
  • Collaborate with fabrication and production teams to coordinate material flow and meet production deadlines.
  • Adhere to all safety protocols and company policies to maintain a safe working environment.

Skills:

The Cutter - Fabrication utilizes technical skills daily to interpret complex blueprints and translate them into precise cutting actions, ensuring materials meet exact specifications. Attention to detail is essential to minimize errors and material waste, directly impacting production quality and cost efficiency. Proficiency with various cutting tools and machinery allows the Cutter to maintain consistent output while adhering to safety standards. Communication and teamwork skills facilitate effective collaboration with fabrication and production teams to meet deadlines and resolve issues promptly. Additionally, problem-solving abilities help the Cutter adjust processes or equipment settings to optimize performance and address any challenges encountered during cutting operations.

title: Systems Engineer, Journeyman
description:
Systems engineering is essential to ensuring Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) capabilities remain technically sound, interoperable, resilient, and capable of supporting the nation's strategic deterrence mission. Sumaria Systems is seeking a Journeyman Systems Engineer to support the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC), Program Executive Office Nuclear Command, Control and Communications (PEO NC3) mission at Hanscom AFB, Massachusetts.

The ideal candidate has experience working within Air Force or Department of Defense technical environments and can translate operational needs into technical requirements, evaluate system performance and engineering alternatives, maintain technical baselines, and coordinate complex engineering activities across Government and mission stakeholders.

In this role, you will apply systems engineering principles to NC3 acquisition, modernization, integration, sustainment, and mission-worthiness activities. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Apply systems engineering principles and methodologies throughout the system lifecycle.

  • Support engineering analysis of current and future systems within the NC3 mission architecture.

  • Develop, analyze, integrate, maintain, and update system and technical requirements.

  • Support requirements management and traceability to ensure operational needs are accurately reflected in system and subsystem requirements.

  • Establish, manage, and evaluate program technical baselines.

  • Review system and subsystem designs for consistency with approved specifications, interfaces, performance criteria, and mission requirements.

  • Support system integration, verification, validation, and system-level testing.

  • Review engineering and test results, identify technical deficiencies and risks, and recommend corrective actions.

  • Conduct technical research and data analysis supporting NC3 system requirements, modernization efforts, acquisition activities, and mission-worthiness assessments.

  • Evaluate new technologies, architectures, requirements, and system concepts for potential impacts to existing and future NC3 capabilities.

  • Conduct or support engineering trade studies, technical assessments, and analysis of alternatives to inform Government decisions.

  • Identify technical risks, dependencies, and integration challenges and develop recommendations for mitigation or resolution.

  • Support Digital Engineering and Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) activities as applicable to assigned systems and programs.

  • Support configuration management and change-control activities to maintain the integrity of system requirements and technical baselines.

  • Coordinate engineering activities across modeling and simulation, cybersecurity, configuration management, logistics, acquisition, and other technical disciplines.

  • Participate in technical reviews, program reviews, Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), working groups, and other engineering forums.

  • Develop technical documentation, diagrams, presentations, analyses, briefings, and other decision-support products.

  • Communicate technical findings, risks, alternatives, and recommendations to Government and program leadership.

Required Skills/Education

Education: Bachelor's Degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Relevant systems engineering experience may be considered in lieu of degree requirements where permitted by the contract.

Years of Experience: Five (5) or more years of relevant systems engineering, system integration, technical analysis, acquisition engineering, or related Department of Defense engineering experience.

Required Qualifications:

  • Experience applying systems engineering principles within complex technical environments.

  • Experience with requirements development, analysis, management, and traceability.

  • Experience evaluating system or subsystem designs, interfaces, performance, and technical requirements.

  • Experience supporting system integration, verification, validation, or system-level testing.

  • Understanding of technical baseline development and configuration management.

  • Ability to evaluate technical alternatives, identify engineering risks, and develop recommendations.

  • Experience developing and reviewing technical documentation, engineering analyses, briefings, and decision-support products.

  • Understanding of system development and acquisition lifecycle activities.

  • Strong analytical and technical problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary Government and contractor engineering teams.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience supporting the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center, PEO NC3, or related NC3 programs.

  • Experience supporting Air Force acquisition programs at Hanscom AFB.

  • Experience with NC3, strategic communications, SATCOM, C5ISR, or other mission-critical communications systems.

  • Experience with Air Force or DoD systems engineering and acquisition processes.

  • Experience conducting technical reviews, trade studies, system performance assessments, or Analysis of Alternatives.

  • Experience with Digital Engineering, Digital Thread, Digital Twin, or Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE).

  • Familiarity with SysML or related architecture and systems modeling methodologies.

  • Experience with requirements-management tools and processes.

  • Experience supporting mission-worthiness, readiness, or system-effectiveness assessments.

Travel: Limited travel may be required in support of program objectives.

Security Clearance Required: Tier 5 / Current Top Secret Security Clearance.

Position Type: Full Time

Salary: $115K - $125K

title: Senior System Engineer (Virtual Private Cloud Team)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior System Engineer (Virtual Private Cloud Team) based in France.

This is a senior systems engineering role focused on building and operating the core networking layer of a large-scale cloud platform.
You will work on virtual private networking that enables reliable connectivity across distributed datacenter environments.
The role combines high-level control-plane development in Go with low-level dataplane and systems engineering, primarily involving C and open-source technologies.
You will contribute to secure networking services including virtual networks, load balancers, firewalls, security groups, and connectivity features.
A key focus will be improving scalability, resilience, performance, and stability across critical cloud infrastructure.
You will investigate challenging networking, datapath, kernel, and performance issues while collaborating with experienced engineers across the platform.
This is an opportunity to work on foundational infrastructure where your engineering decisions directly influence the reliability of cloud services.

Accountabilities

  • Develop and operate the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networking layer that provides reliable connectivity for cloud workloads.
  • Design and implement scalable and resilient networking services for virtualized cloud environments.
  • Develop and maintain the control plane, primarily using Go.
  • Contribute to the development and integration of dataplane components, primarily written in C and based on open-source networking technologies.
  • Improve the scalability, reliability, and operational stability of core cloud networking services.
  • Develop networking functionality such as IPv6 support, service endpoints, VPC peering, and Layer 7 load balancing.
  • Contribute to the development and improvement of network services including load balancers, firewalls, and security groups.
  • Improve internal architecture and optimize interactions between VPC services and related cloud platform components.
  • Investigate and resolve complex datapath and Linux kernel networking issues.
  • Analyze and address networking performance bottlenecks at both system and application levels.
  • Design and execute load and performance testing for cloud networking services.
  • Debug complex issues involving routing, connectivity, concurrency, and distributed infrastructure.
  • Develop reliable, high-performance, concurrent systems code suitable for large-scale production environments.
  • Contribute to the resilience of cloud networking infrastructure so services remain operational during partial system or infrastructure failures.
  • Collaborate with engineers working across control-plane, dataplane, networking, and platform infrastructure components.
  • Participate in technical design discussions and contribute to improvements in the architecture of core networking services.
  • Research and evaluate networking technologies and approaches that can improve platform capabilities and performance.
  • Participate in coding interviews as part of the recruitment process.

    • Requirements:

    • Significant experience in systems engineering, network engineering, infrastructure engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
    • Strong ability to write reliable, efficient, and high-performance concurrent code.
    • Proficiency in Go (Golang).
    • Ability to read and understand C and/or C++, or a strong willingness and ability to develop these skills.
    • Practical understanding of how network traffic is routed through modern networking systems.
    • Strong knowledge of software engineering principles for production-grade systems and infrastructure.
    • Experience troubleshooting complex systems, networking, or performance-related issues.
    • Ability to work effectively with both high-level control-plane software and low-level systems or dataplane components.
    • Strong analytical and debugging skills, with the ability to investigate issues across multiple layers of a networking stack.
    • Understanding of virtual networking and modern cloud networking architectures is highly valuable.
    • Experience with OVS, VPP, DPDK, Linux kernel networking subsystems, or comparable networking dataplanes is a strong advantage.
    • Familiarity with network overlays, Software-Defined Networking (SDN), Network Functions Virtualization (NFV), or Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) is beneficial.
    • Knowledge of network protocols, routing, tunneling, and related networking technologies.
    • Familiarity with BGP and MPLS is an advantage.
    • Ability to understand complex technical architectures and contribute constructively to design decisions.
    • Strong problem-solving skills and a methodical approach to diagnosing infrastructure and networking issues.
    • Comfortable working collaboratively in a highly technical engineering environment.
    • Willingness to learn new technologies and work across different layers of the cloud networking stack.

      • Benefits:

      • Career growth and continuous learning opportunities.
      • Flexibility and significant ownership in your work.
      • Collaborative and innovative engineering culture.
      • Opportunity to work on high-impact cloud and AI infrastructure projects.

title: Senior Legal Business Partner
description:

Ready to be part of the Legal Tech revolution?

DiliTrust combines a strong international presence with an entrepreneurial culture, helping customers across multiple markets digitize and simplify their legal processes.

Your role

As Senior Legal Business Partner, you will act as a trusted legal advisor to DiliTrust’s commercial organization in the United States and Canada. Based in Philadelphia, you will support business growth by leading and negotiating a broad range of commercial agreements, while helping internal stakeholders identify practical and proportionate solutions to legal and business risks.

You will partner closely with Sales, Account Management, Customer Success, Professional Services, Security, Finance, and other business functions. Your role will be both strategic and hands-on: you will manage negotiations directly, improve contracting processes, and help the business close opportunities efficiently while protecting DiliTrust’s interests.

  • Lead the drafting, review, negotiation, and execution of commercial agreements for DiliTrust’s US and Canadian markets.

  • Develop and maintain contract templates, negotiation playbooks, fallback positions, and approval guidelines to streamline deal execution.

Your Profile

  • US-qualified attorney with several years of experience in commercial, technology, SaaS, or in-house legal roles.

  • Experience supporting sales teams and advising business stakeholders in a fast-paced, international environment.
  • Strong understanding of SaaS contracts, technology transactions, data protection, intellectual property, and commercial risk.

title: Financial Risk & Strategy Director
description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

U.S. Bancorp Fixed Income, Currencies & Commodities (FICC) is building out a newly created Financial Risk & Strategy function to provide dedicated front-line risk management, financial resource management, and strategic oversight across the FICC businesses, including Macro (Rates / FX), Structured Credit, Working Capital Finance, Debt Capital Markets, Credit, and Commodities. This build-out coincides with U.S. Bancorp's transition across the Category II regulatory asset threshold and the integration of BTIG LLC's equities and prime brokerage capabilities, creating a highly visible mandate at the intersection of risk, finance, and strategy within Global Capital Markets.

POSITION OVERVIEW

Reporting to the Head of FICC Financial Risk & Strategy, the Director will lead strategic analysis and financial resource management initiatives across FICC businesses, including balance sheet allocation, funds transfer pricing, and broker-dealer capital and funding. This role partners closely with Corporate Treasury and Finance to ensure FICC's capital, funding, and liquidity resources are deployed efficiently against strategic priorities.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Capital, Funding & Strategic Analysis

  • Support the FICC Balance Sheet Council, including balance sheet allocation, funding/liquidity analysis, and cross-LOB governance

  • Drive the build-out of G-SIB-standard P&L attribution capabilities, including consistent desk- and product-level decomposition of revenues, carry, funding, hedging, valuation adjustments, and key risk drivers

  • Develop capital attribution and allocation methodologies across FICC desks and products to support transparent risk-adjusted performance measurement, resource optimization, and strategic decision-making

  • Drive broker-dealer capital and funding analysis, including net capital frameworks (SEC Rule 15c3-1) and unsecured funding strategy

  • Partner with Corporate Treasury on FTP methodology, Section 23A lending, and holdco term debt analysis

  • Support preparation of rating agency materials and BTIG integration workstreams from a strategy and financial resource lens

  • Lead or contribute to strategic initiatives such as the FICC Junior Talent Program and other franchise-building efforts

Planning, Reporting & Regulatory Impact

  • Prepare balance sheet planning submissions and cross-LOB dashboards for senior management and planning cycles

  • Analyze regulatory developments (Category II transition, LCR/NSFR, AOCI/CET1) for their impact on FICC's financial resources

QUALIFICATIONS

Basic Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in financial resource management, treasury, corporate development, or strategy within capital markets or banking

  • Strong understanding of balance sheet management, funds transfer pricing, and regulatory capital/liquidity frameworks (LCR, NSFR, CET1)

  • Experience with broker-dealer capital frameworks (SEC Rule 15c3-1) a plus

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or CFA designation preferred

  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, with the ability to synthesize complex regulatory and financial topics into clear, decision-ready materials

  • FINRA Series 7 and 63 licenses required, or ability to obtain within a defined onboarding period

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience preparing materials for senior management and governance committees

Preferred Skills / Experience

  • Advanced degree or CFA designation

  • Experience with broker-dealer capital, funding, and liquidity frameworks

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base pay for this role usually falls within $250,000 to $300,000. Additional considerations regarding base pay levels are based on candidate qualifications. Your compensation expectations will be discussed with a U.S. Bank recruiter if you are contacted to discuss the role further.

That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:

title: Senior ML Engineer (AI Research)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior ML Engineer (AI Research) based in France.

This is a senior-level machine learning engineering role focused on applied AI research and the development of advanced intelligent systems.
You will work on research problems spanning reinforcement learning, agentic systems, reasoning models, web-scale data, and efficient model training.
The role combines rigorous experimentation with strong software engineering and large-scale model development.
You will design and execute research experiments, investigate new approaches, and translate promising findings into practical AI capabilities.
Your work may involve distributed training across multiple compute nodes and modern deep learning frameworks and infrastructure.
You will collaborate with researchers and engineering teams to turn research results into impactful applications and technical contributions.
This is an opportunity to work on challenging AI problems in a fast-moving, international, research-driven environment.

Accountabilities

  • Conduct applied machine learning research across areas such as guided search, reinforcement learning, agentic systems, reasoning models, and model distillation.
  • Design and execute experiments to identify efficient approaches for training large language models using interaction traces from diverse environments.
  • Explore methods for guided generation and search within model trajectory spaces.
  • Investigate approaches for collecting and mining relevant training data at web scale.
  • Develop efficient methods for incorporating large-scale data into model post-training workflows.
  • Experiment with different reinforcement learning configurations in domains where rewards can be verified.
  • Explore approaches for training AI agents on tasks where reward signals are difficult or impossible to verify directly.
  • Formulate research questions and translate hypotheses into well-designed machine learning experiments.
  • Design experiments with appropriate statistical rigor, ensuring results are reliable, interpretable, and reproducible.
  • Analyze experimental results and identify meaningful conclusions, limitations, and opportunities for further research.
  • Develop and train large-scale machine learning models across multiple computational nodes.
  • Implement research ideas using modern deep learning frameworks, primarily Python and JAX.
  • Translate promising research findings into practical solutions in collaboration with adjacent engineering and research teams.
  • Contribute to technical publications, research reports, and clear documentation of experimental findings.
  • Help shape research directions by identifying promising techniques, evaluating alternatives, and communicating results to technical stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with engineers and researchers to develop scalable systems for experimentation, training, evaluation, and model improvement.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship while contributing hands-on engineering expertise to complex AI research initiatives.
  • Contribute to engineering practices that support reliable and reproducible research, including testing, version control, and continuous integration.

    • Requirements:

    • Significant professional experience in machine learning engineering, applied AI research, or a closely related field, at senior or staff level.
    • Profound understanding of the theoretical foundations of machine learning and reinforcement learning.
    • Deep expertise in modern deep learning for language processing and generation.
    • Substantial experience training large-scale models across multiple computational nodes.
    • Strong software engineering capabilities, particularly with Python.
    • Deep hands-on experience with modern deep learning frameworks, particularly JAX.
    • Strong experience designing, executing, and analyzing machine learning experiments with appropriate statistical rigor.
    • Ability to formulate meaningful research questions, design experiments to test hypotheses, and derive actionable conclusions from results.
    • Strong understanding of experimental methodology, model evaluation, and interpretation of machine learning results.
    • Excellent ability to document technical and research findings clearly and contribute to publications or detailed technical reports.
    • Strong communication, collaboration, and technical leadership skills.
    • Experience with deep reinforcement learning for LLMs, including techniques such as reward modeling, DPO, and PPO, is an advantage.
    • Familiarity with important modern LLM concepts and techniques such as RoPE, ZeRO/FSDP, Flash Attention, and quantization is beneficial.
    • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related discipline; a Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.
    • Track record of building and delivering products or technical systems in a dynamic, startup-like environment is a plus.
    • Experience engineering complex systems such as large-scale distributed data processing platforms or high-load web services is advantageous.
    • Open-source projects demonstrating strong engineering capabilities are a plus.
    • Excellent command of English, with strong technical writing, articulation, and communication skills.
    • Proficiency with contemporary software engineering practices, including CI/CD, version control, and unit testing.
    • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary research and engineering teams.
    • Strong curiosity, analytical thinking, and enthusiasm for solving open-ended and technically challenging AI problems.

      • Benefits:

      • Competitive compensation.
      • Career growth and continuous learning opportunities.
      • Flexibility and significant ownership in your work.
      • Collaborative and innovative research and engineering culture.
      • Opportunity to work on impactful AI research and development projects.
      • Exposure to advanced machine learning, reinforcement learning, LLMs, and agentic AI systems.

title: Product Manager, Agentic Commerce
description:
About VGS

VGS is building the trust infrastructure for a new era of commerce. As commerce becomes agentic, payments are increasing dramatically in volume, speed, and complexity, and the companies driving that shift need a foundation they can fully trust.

That's where VGS comes in. We're the world's leader in payment tokenization, trusted by the most innovative AI and Fortune 500 companies, merchants, banks, and fintechs to power modern payments and agentic commerce. We store more than 9 billion tokens and process more than 10 billion monthly interactions, touching a third of all e-commerce. That scale isn't incidental. It's why leading companies embed our universal token vault and credential management platform directly into their stack, taming the complexity of payment data so they can move faster.

Come build the platform that enables modern payments for the world's largest companies. We're helping businesses unlock new possibilities in an industry that never stops moving. And that takes exceptional people.

About the Role

In this role, you will work with the world’s largest wallets, card networks, and AI/agent platforms. This includes coordinating directly with the networks (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover), and emerging AI commerce and agent-payments providers. You will be focusing on building seamless token APIs, defining and implementing protocols, and trust frameworks that let agents pay securely on behalf of humans. This industry is evolving before our eyes, and you will define what "agent-ready" payments infrastructure looks like before the rest of the industry has agreed on the answer.

What You’ll Do

  • Product Strategy & Discovery: Work directly with partner engineering teams (networks, wallets, AI platforms) to translate emerging standards like Agentic Tokens, ACP, UCP, MPP, etc… into concrete product requirements and roadmaps.

  • Own and drive multi-partner technical integrations end-to-end - you'll be in the weeds with partner engineers, not just handing off specs.

  • Represent VGS in emerging standards conversations, helping define how agent-initiated transactions are authorized, tokenized, and secured across networks.

  • Design browser automation tooling that allow for AI systems to perform human-like interactions in a way that keeps the AI system out of scope with

  • Help build a product point of view on how agentic commerce should work technically, then use that conviction to influence partners and internal engineering roadmaps.

  • Understand, integrate with, and build on top of pre-existing VGS tokenization and payments infrastructure.

What You Bring

  • Experience: 3+ years as a Product Manager, with prior experience in a technically-hands-on role - solutions engineering, technical account management, integration engineering, or software engineering - within payments, fintech, or API platforms.

  • Direct experience delivering APIs, SDKs, or protocols in a partner-facing capacity. You've been the person on the call debugging an integration in real time, and understand what’s needed to fully operationalize a product concept. This includes designing reporting, observability, and other similar systems.

  • Genuine, demonstrated interest in AI/agentic systems - side projects, contributions, or professional work exploring how AI agents interact with external systems.

  • Communication Skills: Comfortable moving between deeply technical partner engineering conversations and executive/GTM conversations about strategy and roadmap.

Mindset:

  • Partner-savvy strategist: You've spent years sitting at the intersection of technical specs and business relationships. This includes interpreting protocol docs, negotiating requirements with vendor and partner teams, and translating product ideas into a roadmap that gets delivered.

  • Curious about the frontier: You're drawn to agentic commerce because it's genuinely unsolved, not just because it's trendy.

  • Technical credibility with product instincts: You can hold your own in a technical design review, but you're increasingly motivated by shaping "what should we build" over "how do we build it.". This means that you can confidently define the differences between various agentic protocols, understand API specs across vendors, and create easy to use interfaces that solve the underlying technical problems rather than giving the issues to the end-consumer to solve.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with tokenization, payment processing, or security products

  • BA/BS degree

  • A knack for out-of-the-box thinking that thrives in a fast-paced startup environment

  • Prior work with AI agent frameworks, LLM tooling, or agent-to-agent protocols.

We're looking for passionate professionals who take pride in their craft and want to help grow a team tackling some of the most critical problems in payments. People who thrive here are curious by nature, unafraid of hard problems, and motivated by the chance to build something that matters at scale.

If you're driven to make a meaningful impact, work at the leading edge of payment technology, and grow your career alongside a team that values ownership, collaboration, and continuous learning, you'll feel right at home at VGS.

How We Work

At VGS, we embrace a remote-first philosophy because we believe flexibility leads to great work and a healthy work-life balance. That said, if you live within 30 miles of one of our office locations, you'll be on a hybrid schedule with some in-person time, because we know there's real value in coming together.

We're not about being in the office every day. We are about connection, collaboration, and the energy that comes from a great brainstorm, a team lunch, or celebrating a big win in person.

Our Benefits

Financial and retirement

  • Competitive salary

  • 401 (k) with a 4% match and immediate vesting (applies to US only)

  • Internet Stipend

  • Learning Stipend

  • Office set-up stipend (applies to US only)

Professional Development

Office life and perks

  • Remote and hybrid opportunities

  • Flexible working hours

  • Weekly office lunches

  • Employee discount platform

Equal Opportunity

Position Summary:
The Airframes Mechanic is responsible for maintaining the exterior aircraft structure and airframe system components for the Customer.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Inspects, maintains, repairs, and services aircraft structure, hydraulic, pneumatic and airframe system components.

2. Performs hourly, calendar, phase, and conditional inspections as required by maintenance requirement cards.

3. Troubleshoots airframe, flight control, and landing gear systems.

4. Uses color-coded charts of aircraft piping and lines.

5. Reads schematic diagrams, shop sketches, clue prints and interpret applicable technical data

6. Use of power tools and precision measuring devices in the maintenance and repair of aircraft.

Qualifications, Knowledge and Skills Required:

1. High school diploma or equivalent.

2. Level I - Four years’ previous experience in aircraft repair.

3. Completion of one or more NAMTGD or equivalent OMA maintenance courses.

4. Experience performing structural repair utilizing sheet metal, fiberglass, and composite materials

5. Thorough knowledge of corrosion control and aircraft painting techniques.

6. Knowledge of naval maintenance publications, maintenance requirement cards, and the ability to document maintenance utilizing the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Information System (NALCOMIS).

Physical and Environmental Requirements:

This position requires normal physical functions. Work may require frequent bending, reaching and climbing. May frequently lift and carry items weighing up to fifty pounds and occasionally lift heavier items with the assistance of other workers. Work may be performed on top or under equipment in cramped or awkward positions. Normal color perception required.

Work Environment (ADA)

May be required to work in areas in the hangar and on the flightline that are noisy and dusty. May be exposed to moderate discomforts, such as heat, cold and wind. May be required to wear personal protective equipment, when applicable.

Individuals subject to this requirement should demonstrate the following qualifications and personal attributes:

a. A comprehensive background in maintenance practices.

b. Fully developed technical skills and experience relevant to their areas of responsibility.
