title: Mechanical Construction Inspector
description:
Organizational Overview

The Modernization Project Office (MPO) is responsible for the engineering, design, cost estimating, scheduling, and project controls on conventional construction projects, including the selection of architectural/engineering firms, contractors and others engaged for these projects.

Position Description

As a member of the Modernization Project Office, the experienced mechanical inspector will inspect commercial plumbing /mechanical/HVAC work associated with new construction and/or renovation work to ensure conformance with contract documents and applicable codes and standards. The ideal candidate will have field experience in construction with an emphasis on HVAC, plumbing, pipe fitting and fire protection.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Preparation of daily narrative reports.
  • Daily verification of work performed and confirmation that materials and workmanship match specifications and shop drawings.
  • Coordination of construction work with facility operations and other stakeholders.
  • Responsible for verification of quality of work and installation in accordance with NYS building codes.
  • Verification of contractor installation methods with contract drawings and specifications.
  • Conformance with contractual safety requirements.

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Bachelors of Science Degree or NICET III certification or a comparable combination of education and experience.
  • 5 or more years’ experience in construction installation and inspection of large scale commercial HVAC units, industrial size chillers and cooling towers, and commercial ductwork.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook).
  • Working knowledge of the latest version of the mechanical and plumbing ICC building codes.
  • Experience testing and trouble shooting HVAC, chiller, cooling tower, and ductwork startup issues typically encountered during construction.
  • Working knowledge of testing methods and criteria for all types of mechanical systems is required.
  • Demonstrated commitment to working safely, acting ethically, and taking personal accountability for operational excellence.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • The ability to work Overtime on weekends or extended hours to accommodate contractor work schedules.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering.
  • 10 or more years’ experience in construction inspection of large scale Commercial HVAC systems within a medical/ researcher/ or pharmaceutical setting.
  • Experience with plumbing, fire sprinkler, steam and general piping systems.
  • ICC Certified Mechanical Inspector.
  • NICET Level II and III Certification.
  • Working knowledge of the latest version of the mechanical and plumbing NYS/ ICC building codes.
  • Knowledge of fire-stopping, fire-rated construction, and/or fire-proofing.
  • OSHA 30-hour training.

Environmental, Safety, and Health, Requirements:

Must meet physical requirements of the position, including but not limited to:

  • Physical coordination and balance
  • Continuous walking/standing
  • Hearing speech and alarms
  • Good near vision; depth perception; normal color vision
  • Heights (high and low hazard)
  • Lifting (up to 40 lbs); frequent bending/twisting
  • Use of vertical ladders (>4 ft)
  • Ability to work in warm and cold environments (outdoors)

Other Information:

Due to the need for unescorted access to controlled areas of the laboratory, this position is limited to U.S. citizens in accordance with site security requirements. A security clearance is not required at this time.

Brookhaven Laboratory is committed to providing fair, equitable and competitive compensation. This is a multi-level role and the full salary range for this position is $92,050 - $156,150 / year. You will be placed at the level and salary commensurate with your experience. Salary offers will be commensurate with the final candidate's qualification, education and experience and considered with the internal peer group.


Brookhaven National Laboratory is committed to employee success and we believe that a comprehensive employee benefits program is an important and meaningful part of the compensation employees receive. Review more information at BNL | Benefits Program


Brookhaven National Laboratory requires all non-badged personnel including visitors to produce a REAL-ID or REAL-ID compliant documentation to access Brookhaven National Laboratory – view more information at . This is due to nationwide identification requirements for federal site access as required by the federal REAL ID Act. Those not in possession of a REAL ID-compliant document will not be permitted to access the site which includes access to the Laboratory for interviews.


As a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory, Brookhaven National Laboratory requires employees to obtain and maintain a DOE Uncleared Personal Identity Verification (UPIV) credential in accordance with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements. The credentialing process is completed as part of onboarding and enables access to DOE facilities and information systems. As a condition of employment, the selected candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a UPIV credential. These requirements are established under DOE Order 206.2 Chg. 2, Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM- Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM)), and DOE Order 473.1A- Physical Protection Program- Physical Protection Program.


About Us

Brookhaven National Laboratory (www.bnl.gov) delivers discovery science and transformative technology to power and secure the nation’s future. Brookhaven Lab is a multidisciplinary laboratory with seven Nobel Prize-winning discoveries, 37 R&D 100 Awards, and more than 70 years of pioneering research. The Lab is primarily supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science. Brookhaven Science Associates (BSA) operates and manages the Laboratory for DOE. BSA is a partnership between Battelle and The Research Foundation for the State University of New York on behalf of Stony Brook University. BSA salutes our veterans and active military members with careers that leverage the skills and unique experience they gained while serving our country, learn more at BNL | Opportunities for Veterans at Brookhaven National Laboratory.


Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer

Guided by our core values of integrity, responsibility, innovation, respect, and teamwork, Brookhaven Science Associates is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer-Vets/Disabled. We are committed to fostering a respectful and collaborative environment that fuels scientific discovery. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by law. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. *VEVRAA Federal Contractor

title: Adjunct - Electrical Engineering Instructor
description:
Electrical Engineering

Adjunct Faculty Pool | John R. Post School of Engineering | Reading, Pennsylvania

The John R. Post School of Engineering at Alvernia University invites applications to its adjunct faculty pool in Electrical Engineering. We seek professionals to teach both lecture and laboratory courses in person in Reading, Pennsylvania. Most engineering courses are taught at the John R. Post Center, 401 Penn Street, Reading, PA, with some activities potentially using other Alvernia Reading locations. Applicants must be available for weekday daytime teaching, primarily between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. This daytime availability is an important requirement for these in-person positions. Lecture courses typically meet on multiple days each week, so applicants must be able to commit to a recurring weekday schedule for the full semester. Remote or hybrid teaching is not available for these pools. Hired candidates join the adjunct pool and may receive separate contracts for individual courses as needs arise. Pool appointment does not guarantee a course assignment.

Program accreditation

The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the commission's General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s), and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Potential teaching areas

Circuits and Electronics

Circuit theory, analog electronics, electronic devices, electronic design, electrical measurements, and circuits and electronics laboratories.

Digital Systems and Automation

Digital logic and design, embedded and microcontroller-based systems, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), industrial controls, and related laboratory instruction.

Electromagnetics and Electromechanical Energy Conversion

Engineering electromagnetics, electric machines, electromechanical energy conversion, and related electrical energy systems.

Instrumentation, Measurement, and Control Systems

Instrumentation, sensors, data acquisition, measurement and dynamic response, control systems, robotics, mechatronics, and laboratory instruction.

Electrical Engineering Design and Advanced Topics

Engineering design, capstone, and upper-level electrical engineering electives.

Preferred qualifications

We particularly welcome practicing engineers and technical professionals who can bring current industry experience into the classroom. Prior college teaching is not required. Preferred candidates will have at least a master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a closely related field and approximately five or more years of relevant professional experience. These are preferred qualifications, not absolute minimums; comparable combinations of advanced education, professional licensure, specialized expertise, industry experience, research, and teaching will be considered. Completion of the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam, Engineer in Training (EIT) certification, and/or Professional Engineer (PE) licensure is a plus.

Application and employment requirements

How to apply

All applications and application materials must be submitted through Alvernia University's ADP employment portal for the specific adjunct pool posting. Submit a current resume or curriculum vitae and a brief letter of interest identifying the courses or subject areas you believe you are qualified to teach. Do not email application materials. Email inquiries are welcome, but a formal application through ADP is required for consideration.

Work authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States and able to accept employment with Alvernia University without current or future employer sponsorship.

Questions and inquiries

Prospective applicants may contact Dr. Joseph M. Mahoney, Chair of the John R. Post School of Engineering, at joseph.mahoney@alvernia.edu with questions about the School, the adjunct pool, or potential teaching needs. Application materials must be submitted through ADP and should not be emailed.

Equal employment opportunity

Alvernia University is an equal-opportunity employer committed to Franciscan values. People of all faith backgrounds, as well as people with no faith affiliation, are welcome and encouraged to apply. All employees share responsibility for advancing a culture of care in the performance of their roles while demonstrating service orientation, respect for all, intellectual curiosity, solution focus and innovation, and mutual accountability. Alvernia University strives to be a community supportive of diverse perspectives and identities.
